title: Kuku Sabzi (Persian Herb Frittata)
cuisine_note: Kuku sabzi is nearly an herb omelet: eggs bind a mountain of chopped green herbs, a spoon of flour keeps it sliceable, and it is meant to be eaten at room temperature - a Persian picnic and fridge-clearing dish.

qty.note: a large handful - the herbs are the dish, so use the bunch that needs using

steps.text: Set the oven to 375°F. Chop the parsley, cilantro, and dill coarsely - the pieces should read as green confetti, not pesto.
Whisk the eggs with the flour, turmeric, salt, and pepper in the mixing bowl until no flour lumps remain.
Fold in the herbs and green onions. The mix should look more green than yellow; add another handful of chopped herbs if it does not.
Heat the oil in the ovenproof skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes, then pour in the egg mixture and spread it level.
Cook for 4 minutes, until the edges set and lift easily with a spatula while the center still moves.
Transfer the pan to the oven and bake for 12 minutes, until the center is just set and puffed. The center reads 160°F (71°C) on a thermometer.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Rest the kuku in the pan for 10 minutes - it firms as it cools and releases its edges.
Slice into wedges. Kuku eats warm or at room temperature, and it is better the next day; keep wedges covered in the fridge.
